source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Sterling NVA8 campus publishes 24 MW of IT capacity, about 1.5 percent of Virginia's disclosed data center load, which places it well below the state's largest sites.

The facility pairs that 24 MW with 154,230 square feet of technical space. At 40 kW per rack, a density common for AI training, that footprint implies roughly 600 racks. The operator publishes no certifications for the campus, so nothing in the record states what workloads it is qualified to host.

Virginia's disclosed capacity is concentrated. Of 330 mapped facilities in the state, only 25 publish power figures, totaling 1,603 MW, and Sterling ranks 17th among them. Most facilities disclose nothing, so the state's real total is larger than any figure here.

What this does not cover is the part that matters most for AI scaling. The data gives capacity and floor area but no power supply, cooling design, or grid interconnect, so it cannot say whether the site can support dense GPU clusters. It also omits announced expansion, which the suitability score lists as a missing input.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
